notes: Two bounded properties of the gate, named rather than failed, both written into migration 0115's own comment: a change of period costs one pass the gate does not hold, since a record made on another scale serves nothing — for the reference-excerpt loop that is one extra pass at each convergence, and the pass claims nothing, so the cost is a repeated batch of excerpt writes rather than a wrong one; and a period bounds work at one pass per aligned period rather than per arbitrary window, so two passes can fall seconds apart across a boundary. For the GitHub rate limit the leases were chosen against, the per-period bound is the one that matters.

A third, smaller: the scale equality is on the period's nanoseconds, so two builds of a roll that disagree about an interval for one lease would each run their own passes until the roll ends. Bounded by the roll and by the lease's mutual exclusion.
